refutedOnReview: REFUTED as a dialect grouping, though the underlying "no port" observation survives per model.  Sources exist but do not say what is claimed: - The cited Everest 1100 Global Manual (https://www.energizersolar.com/s/Everest-1100-GLOBAL-Manual-zc93.pdf) is real and names ONLY "Everest 1100". It names none of the other 10 models. Per the skill's rule, a vendor doc that does not name the model does not support the claim
gotchas: The Everest manual has no Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or app section at all — checked, not assumed. State of charge appears only as a percentage on the front LCD.
Everest 1100 is 54000 mAh / 21.6 V = 1166 Wh. The model number is watts of AC output, same trap as the Peak line.

Everest and Peak are BOTH Energizer Solar portable power stations from the same licensee, and they differ on the one thing that matters: Peak has Wi-Fi/Tuya, Everest has nothing. Do not generalise from one to the other.
